content.title: The Cost of Privacy in Fair Machine Learning
content.abstract: A common task in fair machine learning is training ML models that preserve certain summary statistics across subpopulations defined by sensitive attributes. However, access to such sensitive attributes in training data is restricted and the learner must rely on noisy proxies for the sensitive attributes. In this paper, we study the effect of a privacy mechanism that obfuscates the sensitive attributes from the learner on the fairness of the resulting classifier. We show that the cost of privacy in fair ML is a decline in the generalizability of fairness constraints.
